testcases.title: Identifiers Keywords Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates proper Verilog identifier naming conventions, valid keyword usage, and comment styles. Shows examples of valid identifiers (alphanumeric, underscores, CamelCase) alongside invalid patterns (starting with numbers, containing hyphens/spaces, reserved characters) to illustrate lexical rules.

testcases.title: Number Formats Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates all Verilog number format syntaxes including binary, decimal, hexadecimal, and octal representations. Shows proper use of bit-width specification, base indicators, underscores for readability, and both sized and unsized number literals in both design and testbench contexts.

testcases.title: Strings Escape Sequences Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates string literals, escape sequences, and special characters in Verilog, showing how strings are stored in reg types with 8 bits per character and how common escape sequences (\n, \t, \\ , \") are used in both design and testbench modules.

testcases.title: Buggy Lexical Conventions Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A Verilog module demonstrating identifier naming conventions and bit manipulation operations that contains a syntax error in a continuous assignment statement. The module uses various naming styles (camelCase, snake_case, leading underscore) and performs XOR, masking, and shifting operations, but fails to compile due to incomplete statement syntax.

testcases.title: Buggy Lexical Conventions Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A module demonstrating number format literals (binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal) for encoding and decoding operations. The design contains syntax errors and incomplete logic that prevent proper compilation and functional correctness.

testcases.title: Buggy Identifiers Keywords Example Ex1
testcases.scenario: Priority encoder module with subtle bugs in identifier naming conventions and logic. The exercise contains multiple issues: unsafe identifier usage (starting with underscore), incorrect operator precedence in combinational logic, logic inversion errors, and incomplete module instantiation in the testbench.

testcases.title: Buggy Identifiers Keywords Example Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise contains multiple bugs in a decoder-multiplexer design with identifier naming issues and incomplete module definitions. Students must identify syntax errors, malformed signal declarations, and incomplete module instantiation to make the code synthesizable.

testcases.title: Buggy Number Formats Example Ex1
testcases.scenario: ALU module demonstrating number format usage (binary, hex, decimal) with incomplete implementation containing syntax and logic errors. The module is truncated mid-case statement and has inconsistent number format conventions that cause compilation failures.

testcases.title: Buggy Number Formats Example Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates number format handling bugs including incorrect BCD-to-binary conversion formula, inverted max/min value assignment logic in the comparator, and an incomplete Gray code converter implementation. Students must identify and fix the mathematical calculation error, logical inversion, and syntax incompleteness.

testcases.title: Buggy Strings Escape Sequences Examp Ex1
testcases.scenario: This buggy exercise contains string literals in Verilog and an incomplete conditional statement in the ascii_processor module. The message_formatter stores 16-character strings in registers, while ascii_processor is supposed to convert ASCII characters to uppercase/lowercase and identify alpha and digit characters, but the implementation is truncated mid-statement.

testcases.title: Buggy Strings Escape Sequences Examp Ex2
testcases.scenario: A character FIFO module with ASCII case conversion that incorrectly uses 8'h21 instead of 8'h20 for the XOR bit mask to convert lowercase letters to uppercase. The bug causes incorrect character transformation (e.g., 'a' becomes 'b' instead of 'A') when writing data through the FIFO.

testcases.title: Nets Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates different net types in Verilog (wire, wand, wor, tri, triand, trior) and their resolution functions when multiple drivers are connected. This example illustrates the fundamental differences between combinational nets and specialized multi-driver nets with AND/OR resolution semantics.

testcases.title: Registers Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental Verilog register data types (reg, integer, real, time) and their declarations, showing both unsigned and signed variants with appropriate bit widths for different simulation purposes.

testcases.title: Vectors Arrays Memories Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates vector declarations with various bit widths, array usage for memory modeling, and indexing/slicing operations in Verilog. This example establishes foundational understanding of how to declare and manipulate multi-bit data structures in hardware design.

testcases.title: Parameters Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates parameter and localparam declarations in Verilog, showing how to create configurable, reusable designs with compile-time constants. Parameters can be overridden during instantiation for design flexibility, while localparams provide internal constants that cannot be modified.

testcases.title: Buggy Data Types Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A traffic light controller that uses reg and wire data types to manage state transitions and output signals. The design contains intentional bugs in data type assignments and logic that prevent correct operation of the state machine and output signal generation.

testcases.title: Buggy Data Types Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A configurable FIFO-style buffer that implements write/read pointers and count tracking using vectors and parameters. The design is incomplete with missing count logic that fails to properly track the number of elements in the buffer.

testcases.title: Buggy Nets Example Ex1
testcases.scenario: Bus arbiter with multi-driver nets (wand, wor, tri) and tristate bus multiplexer. Tests proper use of net types for concurrent signal driving and high-impedance bus resolution.

testcases.title: Buggy Nets Example Ex2
testcases.scenario: A traffic signal controller demonstrating wire, wand, wor, and tri net types for combining sensor inputs and resolving priority between N-S and E-W traffic demands. The design contains bugs in net assignments and incomplete conditional logic that prevent correct signal generation.

testcases.title: Buggy Registers Example Ex1
testcases.scenario: A multi-stage data pipeline using various register types (reg, integer, real, time) for processing, accumulation, and timing measurements. The code contains incomplete logic and missing statements that prevent proper pipeline operation and data flow through three processing stages.

testcases.title: Buggy Registers Example Ex2
testcases.scenario: A byte framing unit that collects serial nibbles into bytes and accumulates checksums using various register data types (reg, integer). The design has incomplete implementation and logic errors in the nibble collection and checksum accumulation logic that students must identify and fix.

testcases.title: Buggy Vectors Arrays Memories Exampl Ex1
testcases.scenario: A synchronous FIFO implementation using arrays for memory storage and vectors for data paths. The code contains a syntax error in the read operation that truncates the pointer variable name, preventing proper data retrieval from the FIFO memory.

testcases.title: Buggy Vectors Arrays Memories Exampl Ex2
testcases.scenario: A dual-port register file and histogram unit that demonstrate vector slicing, 2D arrays, and memory operations. Students must identify bugs in synchronous read behavior, incomplete histogram implementation, and vector operations.

testcases.title: Buggy Parameters Example Ex1
testcases.scenario: A configurable timer and watchdog system using parameters for width, divisor, and timeout values. The exercise contains bugs in parameter usage, bit-width handling, and incomplete initialization logic that students must identify and fix.

testcases.title: Buggy Parameters Example Ex2
testcases.scenario: This parameterized ALU module performs addition, subtraction, bitwise AND, and left shift operations with overflow detection. The design uses parameters to configure data width and shift depth, but contains a critical bug in how the shift amount is computed.

testcases.title: All Operators Example
testcases.scenario: Comprehensive demonstration of all fundamental Verilog operators including arithmetic, relational, logical, bitwise, reduction, shift, concatenation, conditional, and replication operators. This module and testbench showcase proper syntax and expected behavior for each operator category.

testcases.title: Buggy Verilog Operators Exercise1
testcases.scenario: An 8-bit ALU module that performs arithmetic, logical, and shift operations with flag generation. The code contains intentional operator bugs in the conditional logic and incomplete flag assignments that produce incorrect results.

testcases.title: Buggy Verilog Operators Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A bit manipulation module demonstrating reduction operators, concatenation, replication, and conditional operators in Verilog. The exercise includes a sign extension module and incomplete top-level wrapper that students must debug.

testcases.title: Verilog Blocks Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental Verilog block constructs including sequential blocks (begin-end), parallel blocks (fork-join), named blocks, the disable statement, and nested block hierarchies. Provides practical examples of how statements execute in different block types with timing behavior.

testcases.title: Buggy Verilog Blocks Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This Verilog packet parser exercise demonstrates the use of named sequential blocks, nested block structures, and disable statements for error handling. The incomplete code contains a syntax error that prevents compilation, specifically in the assignment section of the active_block.

testcases.title: Buggy Verilog Blocks Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A round-robin task scheduler module with named blocks and Verilog tasks for queue management. The design uses enqueue and dequeue tasks with named blocks to manage a priority task queue, but the code is incomplete and contains syntax errors.

testcases.title: Compiler Directives Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates compiler directives including `timescale for simulation precision, `define for parameterization and macros, and conditional compilation with `ifdef/`else/`endif for feature control and simulation modes.

testcases.title: Buggy Compiler Directives Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A configurable digital filter using compiler directives for feature selection and parameterization. The exercise demonstrates `define, `ifdef, `ifndef, `timescale, and `default_nettype directives, but the design is incomplete with truncated module logic and instantiation.

testcases.title: Buggy Compiler Directives Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A protocol encoder with compile-time configuration using `ifdef directives for parity selection. The encoder's calc_parity function has swapped branches—when PARITY_EVEN is defined, it returns inverted parity (~p) instead of correct even parity (p), causing the decoder to flag all valid frames as parity errors.

testcases.title: Parameters Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates Verilog parameter fundamentals including parameter declaration, localparam usage, parameter overriding at instantiation, and parameterized module design. Shows how parameters enable module reusability across different configurations while localparam restricts overriding to internal constants.

testcases.title: Buggy Parameters In Verilog Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A parameterized LIFO stack module with configurable data width and depth uses an incorrect MAX_COUNT calculation (DEPTH+1 instead of DEPTH), causing the full flag to trigger at the wrong stack occupancy level. This exercises parameter/localparam usage and how derived parameters must correctly reference their source values.

testcases.title: Buggy Parameters In Verilog Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A parameterized timer module that supports multiple modes (freerun, oneshot, PWM) with configurable width and prescaler, but the implementation has critical syntax errors preventing compilation and missing logic for timer operation.

testcases.title: Strength Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates Verilog signal drive strengths (supply, strong, pull, weak, highz) and their specification in gate-level constructs. Illustrates how strength resolution works when multiple drivers contend on a net, and shows practical applications of strength specification in pull-up/pull-down configurations.

testcases.title: Buggy Strength In Verilog Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A bus arbiter module using Verilog strength resolution to prioritize multiple drivers on a shared tri-state bus, where strong vs. weak strengths determine which driver's value dominates when multiple drivers are active simultaneously.

testcases.title: Buggy Strength In Verilog Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Memory cell designs with strength modeling for read/write operations and multi-port bus arbitration. The module instantiates SRAM cells, voltage dividers, and multi-port memory using Verilog strengths to resolve contention, but contains syntax errors that prevent compilation.

testcases.title: Data Types In Sv
testcases.scenario: Comprehensive demonstration of SystemVerilog data types including 2-state types (bit, byte, shortint, int, longint) for simulation efficiency and 4-state types (logic, reg, integer, time) for hardware modeling with X and Z states. Establishes foundational understanding of type selection, memory efficiency, and semantic correctness in verification environments.

testcases.title: Exercise 1
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog module that converts between various data types with signed/unsigned arithmetic and uses enums/typedefs for mode selection and status reporting. The source file is incomplete, cutting off mid-parameter declaration in the module definition.

testcases.title: Exercise 2
testcases.scenario: Type-aware ALU that performs arithmetic operations on different data formats using SystemVerilog type definitions and enums. The design demonstrates how incorrect type casting ($unsigned instead of $signed) causes negative operands to be misinterpreted as large positive values during signed arithmetic operations.

testcases.title: Basic Gates Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental gate-level modeling in Verilog using primitive gate instantiations (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR). Shows proper port ordering with output first, instance naming conventions, and synthesis of basic combinational logic from gate primitives.

testcases.title: Buggy Gate Level Modeling Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A 2-to-4 decoder and 4-bit priority encoder implemented using gate-level primitives. The decoder has a bug in y2's logic, and the priority encoder module is incomplete with a syntax error in the q1 OR gate instantiation.

testcases.title: Buggy Gate Level Modeling Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A 4-bit ripple carry adder built from gate-level full adders with conditional inversion for subtraction mode. The design demonstrates gate-level arithmetic logic but contains intentional bugs in the implementation.

testcases.title: Continuous Assignments Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental data flow modeling techniques using continuous assignments in Verilog, including arithmetic operations, bitwise logic, multiplexing, and concatenation. Shows how combinational logic can be expressed abstractly through assign statements where outputs continuously reflect input changes.

testcases.title: Buggy Data Flow Modeling Exercise1
testcases.scenario: An 8-bit barrel shifter using continuous assignments that supports shift left, shift right, rotate left, and rotate right operations. The design contains a critical bug in the rotate right operation that causes incorrect data flow through the bitwise operations.

testcases.title: Buggy Data Flow Modeling Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A BCD to 7-segment decoder and single-digit BCD adder using continuous assignments. The exercise contains multiple intentional bugs in data flow logic, including incorrect BCD validation ranges, missing module port declarations, and improper carry logic in the BCD adder.

testcases.title: Always Blocks Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates behavioral modeling in Verilog using always blocks for both combinational logic (always @(*)) and sequential logic (always @(posedge clk)), including procedural assignments, event controls, and common design patterns like multiplexers, counters, and ALUs.

testcases.title: Buggy Behavioral Modeling Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A vending machine FSM using always blocks and case statements that dispenses an item when 15 cents is accumulated. The code contains a syntax error that prevents compilation and incomplete state machine logic.

testcases.title: Buggy Behavioral Modeling Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A PWM generator module with behavioral modeling using always blocks that contains logic errors in the duty cycle comparison and a syntax error in the duty_cycle_measurer module. The PWM output should pulse high for a configurable duty cycle within a period, but the comparison logic incorrectly uses <= instead of < causing incorrect pulse width.

testcases.title: Switch Level Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental switch-level modeling in Verilog using MOS transistors (nmos, pmos, cmos) and bidirectional switches (tran, tranif). This example illustrates the lowest abstraction level for circuit design, showing how transistor-level behavior including signal strength and charge storage is modeled at the switch level.

testcases.title: Buggy Switch Level Modeling Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This switch-level modeling exercise implements an XOR gate and full adder using CMOS transistor-level primitives (pmos, nmos switches). The incomplete code defines inverter, NAND2, NOR2, AND2, and OR2 gates but is missing the XOR gate module and the main switch_xor_gate adder that the testbench instantiates.

testcases.title: Buggy Switch Level Modeling Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Implements a 6-transistor SRAM cell using switch-level primitives with cross-coupled inverter storage, access transistors, and precharge/sense amplifier circuits. The testbench attempts to verify write and read operations across multiple memory addresses, but the design is incomplete.

testcases.title: Udp Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates user-defined primitives (UDPs) in Verilog, including combinational UDPs (AND, OR, XOR gates) and sequential UDPs with truth tables. Shows how to define primitives with port declarations, truth table specifications, and proper instantiation patterns.

testcases.title: Buggy User-Defined Primitives Exercise1
testcases.scenario: Implements combinational UDPs for a 3-input majority gate, 2-to-1 selector, and full adder primitives, then uses them in a priority encoder/arbiter. The source code is truncated mid-implementation, leaving critical UDP definitions and testbench assertions incomplete.

testcases.title: Buggy User-Defined Primitives Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Incomplete sequential UDP definition for a D flip-flop with asynchronous reset, used in a traffic signal FSM controller. The UDP table entries are missing, preventing the flip-flop from capturing and propagating state changes on clock edges.

testcases.title: Blocking Assignments Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates blocking assignments (=) in combinational always blocks, showing sequential execution where each statement completes before the next executes, allowing downstream statements to use updated values from previous assignments. Covers proper usage patterns in combinational logic and provides multiple examples including priority encoders and ALUs.

testcases.title: Buggy Blocking Assignments Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A multi-stage combinational pipeline using blocking assignments in always @(*) blocks with intentional bugs. The design processes input data through three stages with operations like increment, decrement, bitwise negation, and overflow detection using wide temporary variables.

testcases.title: Buggy Blocking Assignments Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A 4-element sorting network that uses blocking assignments in a combinational always block to implement a bubble sort algorithm with compare-and-swap operations. The design aims to sort four 8-bit inputs and compute min/max values, but contains bugs in the blocking assignment logic or incomplete module definitions.

testcases.title: Non Blocking Assignments Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates proper use of non-blocking assignments (<=) in sequential logic to create a 3-stage pipeline where all register updates execute in parallel, avoiding race conditions and ensuring correct pipeline behavior where each stage captures the previous stage's value from the prior clock cycle.

testcases.title: Buggy Non Blocking Assignments Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A 4-stage FIFO pipeline design that demonstrates non-blocking assignments for pipelined data movement. The code contains a critical bug mixing non-blocking and blocking assignments in the flush logic, and an incomplete code section that prevents compilation.

testcases.title: Buggy Non Blocking Assignments Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Multi-clock domain data synchronizer that synchronizes data across clock domains using a double-register synchronizer with handshake protocol. The design demonstrates CDC (clock domain crossing) techniques but contains a critical bug in the synchronization logic that violates non-blocking assignment rules.

testcases.title: Procedural Timing Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental procedural timing control constructs in Verilog including delay controls (#), event controls (@), and wait statements for synchronizing testbench operations. Illustrates both synthesizable and non-synthesizable timing constructs with practical examples in always blocks and initial blocks.

testcases.title: Buggy Procedural Timing Control Exercise1
testcases.scenario: Watchdog timer with event-driven timeout detection that monitors a heartbeat signal using procedural timing controls. The design incorrectly uses an intra-assignment delay (#20) on the alarm output, causing it to assert much later than test expectations.

testcases.title: Buggy Procedural Timing Control Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Button debouncer module that implements digital filtering using timing control and counter-based state machines. The design uses a synchronizer for metastability protection, a debounce counter to filter glitches, and edge detection to generate clean pulse outputs.

testcases.title: If Statement Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental if-else statement constructs in Verilog, including basic conditionals, if-else-if priority chains, and latch prevention through default assignments. Covers combinational logic synthesis patterns and priority encoding commonly used in digital design.

testcases.title: Buggy If Statement In Verilog Exercise1
testcases.scenario: Traffic light controller using if-else statements for state transitions and pedestrian crossing logic. The source code is incomplete with a truncated if statement, preventing proper state machine implementation and causing compilation failure.

testcases.title: Buggy If Statement In Verilog Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Temperature monitor design with configurable thresholds that uses if-else chains for zone classification and alert generation based on temperature readings. The design implements hysteresis and averaging logic to classify temperatures into zones (cold, normal, warm, hot, critical) and trigger corresponding alerts.

testcases.title: Case Statement Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental case statement variants (case, casez, casex) in Verilog for combinational logic design, including basic arithmetic/logic operations, don't-care handling, and default case usage. Shows proper syntax and best practices for multi-way branching in hardware design.

testcases.title: Buggy Case Statement In Verilog Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This exercise contains a buggy instruction decoder that uses case statements to decode processor instruction opcodes and generate control signals. The source code is incomplete and truncated, cutting off mid-assignment in the always block, making it unable to compile or execute properly.

testcases.title: Buggy Case Statement In Verilog Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A vending machine FSM controller with state transitions, coin processing, and item selection using case statements. The design demonstrates practical FSM implementation but contains a syntax error that prevents compilation.

testcases.title: Loops Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental loop constructs in Verilog including for loops for memory initialization and parity calculation, while loops for sequential operations, and repeat/forever loops for testbenches. This example covers both combinational and sequential loop usage patterns essential for digital design.

testcases.title: Buggy Loops In Verilog Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This design implements a bubble sort network using nested for loops to sort 4 eight-bit values in combinational logic. The source code is incomplete, ending abruptly mid-swap operation, which prevents proper compilation and execution of the sorting algorithm.

testcases.title: Buggy Loops In Verilog Exercise2
testcases.scenario: CRC-8 calculator using for loops for bit-by-bit XOR operations with byte-wise processing. The design demonstrates loop-based bit manipulation and polynomial-based checksum calculation, but the source code is incomplete with syntax errors.

testcases.title: Scheduling Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates Verilog's stratified event queue scheduling model, including active/inactive/NBA/monitor regions, race conditions from simultaneous blocking assignments, delta cycles for combinational settling, and #0 delays for sequencing events within the same timeslot.

testcases.title: Buggy Verilog Scheduling Semantics Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A 4-stage pipeline with mixed blocking and non-blocking assignments that creates scheduling race conditions and data corruption. Stage 1 and Stage 3 use blocking assignments in sequential logic, while Stage 2 uses non-blocking, causing inconsistent timing behavior and invalid data propagation through the pipeline.

testcases.title: Buggy Verilog Scheduling Semantics Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A request-acknowledge handshake synchronizer with data transfer that demonstrates scheduling semantics issues between blocking and non-blocking assignments, and synchronization race conditions. The design attempts to synchronize an external request signal and transfer data across clock domains, but contains critical bugs in both the synchronizer and FSM implementation.

testcases.title: Procedural Continuous Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates procedural continuous assignments using assign/deassign and force/release statements in Verilog. Shows how to override normal procedural assignments in testbenches and the differences between procedural and continuous assignment mechanisms.

testcases.title: Buggy Procedural Continuous Assignments Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A DAC controller that uses procedural continuous assignments (assign/deassign) to override normal DAC output during calibration mode. The design demonstrates testing and override patterns but contains a critical syntax error in the calibration logic block.

testcases.title: Buggy Procedural Continuous Assignments Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A sensor interface module that samples data into a buffer, computes a moving average, and should support fault injection using procedural continuous assignments (assign/deassign). The module demonstrates controlled override of signals for testing purposes.

testcases.title: Module Basics Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental module declaration, port types (input, output, reg, wire), and basic module structure through simple logic gates, registered outputs, and vector arithmetic operations. Illustrates continuous assignments, sequential logic with reset, and multi-module hierarchies.

testcases.title: Port Connection Methods Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates hierarchical module design with multiple port connection methods: positional connections (ordered by port definition), named connections (explicit .port_name syntax), and partial connections. Shows a 4-bit ripple carry adder composed of full adder leaf modules, illustrating how to build complex circuits through module composition.

testcases.title: Buggy Modules And Ports Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A temperature monitoring system with sensor interface, threshold comparator, and alarm controller modules that contains intentional bugs in port connections, module declarations, and logic. The design demonstrates multi-module integration with data scaling, threshold comparison, and alarm control functionality.

testcases.title: Buggy Modules And Ports Exercise2
testcases.scenario: An arithmetic pipeline with multiple sub-modules (adder, multiplier, comparator, mux) connected using named and positional port connections. The design contains intentional bugs in port connections and module instantiation that prevent correct data flow and operation.

testcases.title: Buggy Module Basics Example Ex1
testcases.scenario: A priority encoder system with decoder, mux, and edge detector sub-modules that demonstrates module structure, port declarations, and instantiation. The design contains incomplete module definitions and port mismatches that students must identify and fix.

testcases.title: Buggy Module Basics Example Ex2
testcases.scenario: An alarm system controller module with zone monitoring, siren control, and keypad interface that demonstrates module declaration, port types (input, output, inout), and module hierarchy. The exercise contains syntax and logic errors in the siren_controller module that prevent proper compilation and functionality.

testcases.title: Buggy Port Connection Methods Exampl Ex1
testcases.scenario: A multi-stage datapath module combining an adder, comparator, accumulator, and status logic using various port connection methods (named, positional, and partial connections). The exercise contains incomplete module definitions and port connection bugs that prevent proper hierarchy instantiation and signal passing.

testcases.title: Buggy Port Connection Methods Exampl Ex2
testcases.scenario: A cascaded signal processing pipeline with subtractor, multiplier, limiter, and pipeline register modules that demonstrates named and positional port connections in a hierarchical design. The source code is incomplete with truncated module definitions and testbench initialization, containing syntax errors and missing logic.

testcases.title: Flip Flops Registers Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates fundamental sequential logic elements including D flip-flops with asynchronous and synchronous reset, along with a testbench framework for verifying flip-flop behavior across different reset mechanisms and control signals.

testcases.title: Buggy Implement A Sequential Logic Exercise1
testcases.scenario: PWM generator with configurable duty cycle that implements sequential logic for counter management and PWM output generation. The design generates both complementary PWM outputs with dead-time insertion, but contains a critical syntax error that prevents compilation.

testcases.title: Buggy Implement A Sequential Logic Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UART transmitter with baud rate generator that transmits start bit, 8 data bits, optional parity bit, and stop bit. The design uses a state machine to control transmission sequencing and a baud counter to generate timing for bit transmission.

testcases.title: Tasks Functions Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates task and function declarations with practical examples including basic memory read/write operations, automatic functions with recursion, and utility functions. Illustrates key differences between tasks (timing controls, multiple outputs) and functions (combinational logic, single return value).

testcases.title: Buggy Tasks And Functions Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A packet processor module that uses tasks and functions for packet assembly/disassembly with CRC computation and header validation. The design demonstrates function definitions for CRC-8 calculation, header construction, and validation checks.

testcases.title: Buggy Tasks And Functions Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Matrix operations module with tasks and functions for 2x2 matrix multiply/add operations and determinant calculation. The design contains a critical bug in the determinant function that uses addition instead of subtraction, causing incorrect mathematical results.

testcases.title: Generate Blocks Example
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates parameterized hardware design using generate blocks with three practical examples: ripple-carry adder using generate for loops for bit-parallel instantiation, register file with conditional instantiation, and Gray counter showcasing both generate for and generate if statements for conditional module creation.

testcases.title: Buggy Generate Blocks In Verilog Exercise1

testcases.title: Structures And Unions In Sv

testcases.title: While Loop

testcases.title: Forever Loop

testcases.title: For Loop

testcases.title: Foreach Loop

testcases.title: Repeat Loop

testcases.title: Break And Continue

testcases.title: Named Blocks Statement Labels

testcases.title: Class Assignment In Sv
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the critical distinction between handle assignment and object copying in SystemVerilog classes. testcases.title: An Array Of Objects
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates multiple container types for class objects in SystemVerilog: fixed arrays, dynamic arrays, queues, and associative arrays. Shows proper allocation patterns for each container and iteration using foreach loops.

testcases.scenario: Demonstrates static properties and methods in SystemVerilog classes, showing how static members are shared across all instances of a class and how static methods can only access static data. testcases.title: This Keyword In Classes

This example covers constructor initialization, setter methods that return 'this' for fluent interfaces, and identity/equality checks using 'this'.

testcases.title: Shallow Copy
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates shallow copy behavior in SystemVerilog where object handles are copied but nested objects remain shared between the original and copied instances. Shows that modifying nested object data affects both the original and copy, illustrating the difference between copying handles versus deep cloning.

testcases.title: Deep Copy
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates deep copy implementation in SystemVerilog classes, showing how to recursively copy nested objects to create completely independent instances. Contrasts with shallow copy where nested objects remain shared references.

testcases.title: Inheritance

testcases.title: Super Keyword In Classes

testcases.title: Virtual Keyword In Classes

testcases.title: Abstract Class
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates abstract (virtual) classes and pure virtual methods in SystemVerilog, showing how abstract base classes define interfaces that derived classes must implement while preventing direct instantiation. The example illustrates polymorphic behavior through abstract class handles and the distinction between pure virtual methods (must be implemented) and regular virtual methods (can be overridden with default implementation).

testcases.title: Polymorphism In Sv
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates runtime polymorphism in SystemVerilog through virtual methods and derived classes. Shows how base class handles can reference derived class objects, enabling dynamic method dispatch where the actual method called is determined at runtime based on the object's type.

testcases.title: Scope Resolution Operator
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates SystemVerilog's scope resolution operator (::) for accessing package members, static class variables/methods, and resolving naming conflicts across multiple packages and class hierarchies. The example shows practical usage patterns with math_pkg, string_pkg, and class hierarchies (BaseClass, DerivedClass) to illustrate namespace management and static member access.

testcases.title: Extern Method In Classes
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates extern method definitions in SystemVerilog classes, where method prototypes are declared inside the class while implementations are placed outside using the scope resolution operator. Covers extern constructors, functions, tasks, virtual functions, and static methods.

testcases.title: Parameterized Classes
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates parameterized (generic) classes in SystemVerilog using type and value parameters to create reusable Stack, Register, FIFO, Pair, and Memory class templates. Shows instantiation of parameterized classes with different data types and depths, enabling type-safe, configurable data structure implementations.

testcases.title: Data Encapsulation And Hiding
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates data encapsulation and information hiding in SystemVerilog classes using a BankAccount hierarchy. Shows how local, protected, and public access modifiers control visibility, with getter methods providing secure read access to internal state and validation logic in constructor and setter methods.

testcases.title: Local Access Qualifier
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the 'local' access qualifier in SystemVerilog classes, showing how local members and methods are strictly private to the class and inaccessible even to derived classes. The PasswordManager example illustrates encapsulation best practices by hiding sensitive data (password, hash, failed attempts) behind a public interface.

testcases.title: Protected Access Qualifier
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the 'protected' access qualifier in SystemVerilog classes, showing how protected members and methods are accessible within the declaring class and all derived classes, but remain inaccessible from external code. This example contrasts protected access with public and local qualifiers.

testcases.title: Constant Class Properties
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates SystemVerilog const class properties that enforce immutability—properties initialized at declaration become global constants, while those initialized in constructors become instance-specific constants that cannot be modified after construction. This pattern ensures configuration integrity and prevents accidental mutation of critical values.

testcases.title: Typedef Class In Sv
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates typedef and forward declarations for classes in SystemVerilog, enabling mutual references between classes like Node/LinkedList and self-referencing structures like BinaryTree. Forward declarations allow classes to reference each other before full definition, while typedef creates type aliases for cleaner code organization.

testcases.title: Buggy Classes Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog class hierarchy for geometric shapes demonstrating inheritance, virtual methods, and polymorphism. The code contains multiple bugs in method implementations and syntax that prevent proper instantiation and calculation of shape properties.

testcases.title: Buggy Classes Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Factory pattern implementation with vehicle class hierarchy, static methods, and parameterized garage container. The code contains intentional bugs in class method implementations and inheritance that prevent proper functionality of the vehicle management system.

testcases.title: Buggy Accessing Unallocated Memory Ex1
testcases.scenario: A memory pool manager that allocates and deallocates packet objects, demonstrating null handle checking. The code contains bugs where unallocated memory is accessed without proper null checks, and incomplete function definitions cause compilation failures.

testcases.title: Buggy Accessing Unallocated Memory Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates accessing unallocated memory through null object handles in a SensorNetwork design. The code allocates only 2 of 3 sensors in the SensorHub array, then attempts to access all 3 sensors without null checks, causing a null-dereference crash. Additionally, the SensorNetwork class has incomplete code and uninitialized hub_b.

testcases.title: Buggy Class Assignment In Sv Ex1
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates handle vs object assignment in SystemVerilog classes using a register bank. The code contains intentional bugs where handles are copied instead of performing deep copies of objects, causing unintended aliasing and shared state between supposedly independent instances.

testcases.title: Buggy Class Assignment In Sv Ex2
testcases.scenario: Configuration object management where handles are assigned instead of deep copying, causing unintended sharing of PortConfig objects across SwitchConfig instances. The copy() method in SwitchConfig assigns port handles directly rather than calling the PortConfig copy() method, breaking encapsulation and independence.

testcases.title: Buggy An Array Of Objects Ex1
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog class-based scoreboard maintains an array of ScoreEntry objects. The design allocates the array container but fails to construct individual ScoreEntry objects, causing null pointer dereferences when methods attempt to access object members.

testcases.title: Buggy An Array Of Objects Ex2
testcases.scenario: Queue-based task scheduler using SystemVerilog class arrays and dynamic queues. Implements task management with enqueue/dequeue, priority selection, and completion marking, but contains bugs in array deletion logic and incomplete code.

testcases.title: Buggy Static Properties And Methods Ex1
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog class demonstrates static properties and methods for tracking connection instances and data transmission, but fails to properly reset the instance_count in the reset_stats() function, causing subsequent instance creation to generate incorrect IDs and counts.

testcases.title: Buggy Static Properties And Methods Ex2
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog class design that implements a static device registry to track multiple Device instances with shared counters for ID assignment and active device count. The exercise tests whether static properties and methods correctly maintain global state across multiple instances and registry operations.

testcases.title: Buggy This Keyword In Classes Ex1
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog class exercise demonstrating incorrect usage of the `this` keyword in constructors and methods. The code has inconsistent application of `this` for member variable assignments, causing some assignments to fail (shadowing by local parameters) while others work correctly, creating subtle bugs that affect object initialization and method chaining.

testcases.title: Buggy This Keyword In Classes Ex2
testcases.scenario: A buggy SystemVerilog class demonstrating incorrect use of the 'this' keyword in constructor assignment, method return values for builder pattern chaining, and swap logic. Students must identify where 'this' is missing, where null is incorrectly returned instead of this, and where swap logic fails to preserve values.

testcases.title: Buggy Shallow Copy Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates shallow copy vs. deep copy issues in SystemVerilog classes, where the manual_copy() and clone() methods fail to properly duplicate nested objects like Metadata, causing unintended shared references between copies.

testcases.title: Buggy Shallow Copy Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates shallow copy pitfalls in SystemVerilog classes by implementing a VideoFrame with both shallow and attempted deep copy methods. The bug is that try_deep_copy() copies pixel object handles instead of creating new PixelData objects, leaving shared references that cause unintended aliasing.

testcases.title: Buggy Deep Copy Ex1
testcases.scenario: Deep copy implementation for a protocol message hierarchy with nested objects and arrays. The exercise demonstrates shallow vs. deep copying in SystemVerilog classes and the critical importance of recursively copying all nested objects and containers.

testcases.title: Buggy Deep Copy Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates deep copy failures in a transaction pipeline system where nested objects are not properly cloned, causing unintended aliasing and data corruption. Students must identify bugs in TxnPayload, TxnHeader, and Transaction deep_copy methods that fail to recursively copy all data members.

testcases.title: Buggy Inheritance Ex1
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog class inheritance exercise demonstrating a common bug where the Car class constructor fails to call super.new(), leaving parent class fields (brand, year, fuel) uninitialized. The ElectricCar class correctly calls super.new() but has inconsistent display logic using fuel instead of battery.

testcases.title: Buggy Inheritance Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog inheritance exercise demonstrating employee hierarchy with Manager, Engineer, and Director classes extending Employee. Contains multiple bugs in constructor parameter passing and salary calculation methods that fail to properly implement inheritance semantics.

testcases.title: Buggy Super Keyword In Classes Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates improper use of the super keyword in SystemVerilog class inheritance. The USBDriver class fails to call super.new() in its constructor, leaving inherited fields uninitialized, and the init() method doesn't call super.init(), breaking the initialization chain.

testcases.title: Buggy Super Keyword In Classes Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates the super keyword in SystemVerilog class inheritance, where a three-level protocol stack (L1Proto → L2Proto → L3Proto) uses super to call parent class methods. The L3Proto class fails to properly chain super calls in its constructor, breaking the initialization hierarchy.

testcases.title: Buggy Virtual Keyword In Classes Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates virtual function dispatch in SystemVerilog classes using a shape renderer system. The canvas stores Renderable base class handles that point to derived shape objects (Circle, Rectangle, Triangle), testing whether virtual functions correctly dispatch to derived class implementations.

testcases.title: Buggy Virtual Keyword In Classes Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog class hierarchy with event handlers demonstrating polymorphic behavior. The exercise tests whether handle_event() method is properly overridden in derived classes when called through a base class reference, exposing the absence of the virtual keyword on a critical method.

testcases.title: Buggy Abstract Class Ex1
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog exercise with abstract base class DataFilter and concrete filter implementations (LowPassFilter, ScaleFilter). The ScaleFilter incorrectly adds the factor instead of multiplying, and FilterChain applies filters in reverse order during processing.

testcases.title: Buggy Abstract Class Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog abstract class hierarchy for transport protocols (TCP and UDP) with a mux for broadcasting. The buggy TCPTransport.receive() returns buffer[0] without removing it, causing receive() to always return the same first value instead of advancing through queued data.

testcases.title: Buggy Polymorphism In Sv Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates polymorphism in SystemVerilog through a Zoo class that manages Animal subclasses (Lion, Parrot). The bug involves the speak() method not being declared virtual, causing base-class handle calls to invoke the base implementation instead of the derived override.

testcases.title: Buggy Polymorphism In Sv Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates polymorphism through a codec pipeline system where multiple codec classes (XORCodec, ShiftCodec, AddCodec) override virtual encode/decode methods. The bugs occur in the inverse operations: ShiftCodec.decode() shifts right instead of left, and AddCodec.decode() adds instead of subtracts, breaking the encode-decode roundtrip property.

testcases.title: Buggy Scope Resolution Operator Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates scope resolution in SystemVerilog classes with inheritance. The buggy `show_counts()` method fails to properly access the parent class's static variable, printing the derived class's instance count twice instead of showing both base and derived counts separately.

testcases.title: Buggy Scope Resolution Operator Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog exercise demonstrating scope resolution operators (::) for accessing static members in packages and classes with inheritance. The code contains a critical bug in the scope resolution used within the `find_by_id()` method that prevents proper static member access across the class hierarchy.

testcases.title: Buggy Extern Method In Classes Ex1
testcases.scenario: A FIFO queue implementation using SystemVerilog extern methods with multiple bugs in pointer arithmetic and boundary conditions. The write pointer modulo uses (depth+1) instead of depth, and the is_full() condition incorrectly checks (count>=depth-1) instead of (count>=depth), causing incorrect full/empty detection and pointer wraparound behavior.

testcases.title: Buggy Extern Method In Classes Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise tests extern method definitions in SystemVerilog classes with inheritance. A Router class manages RouterPort objects and their packet transmission. The bug is that the send() method does not increment the packets_sent counter, causing total_sent() to always return 0 despite packets being routed.

testcases.title: Buggy Parameterized Classes Ex1
testcases.scenario: Stack implementation with parameterized type and depth that demonstrates class parameters and stack operations (push, pop, peek). The testbench verifies LIFO behavior, capacity limits, and empty/full conditions.

testcases.title: Buggy Parameterized Classes Ex2
testcases.scenario: A parameterized cache class with configurable data width, tag width, and number of sets. The exercise contains bugs in cache line allocation, hit rate calculation using integer division, and potentially incorrect lookup logic that fails to check the valid bit.

testcases.title: Buggy Data Encapsulation And Hiding Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates encapsulation principles in SystemVerilog classes using a BankAccount example with access control modifiers (local, protected). Students must identify bugs in the implementation where access control and input validation are either missing or incorrectly applied.

testcases.title: Buggy Data Encapsulation And Hiding Ex2
testcases.scenario: A SecureVault class that stores items and requires PIN verification for access, but has multiple encapsulation violations that allow bypassing security checks. The store() function doesn't verify the PIN before storing, change_pin() doesn't verify the old PIN, and item_count is public instead of local.

testcases.title: Buggy Local Access Qualifier Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise tests understanding of the `local` qualifier in SystemVerilog classes. The design implements an authentication manager with password protection and account lockout, but fails to properly restrict access to sensitive members, allowing external code to bypass security mechanisms.

testcases.title: Buggy Local Access Qualifier Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog class exercise demonstrating the consequences of using 'local' instead of 'protected' for inherited member variables. A PremiumWallet subclass cannot access the parent's 'local funds' variable, causing it to silently create a shadow variable initialized to 0, breaking the effective balance calculation.

testcases.title: Buggy Protected Access Qualifier Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates protected access qualifiers in SystemVerilog class hierarchies, where derived classes can access protected members of their base class. The bug occurs in the TempSensor.calibrate() method which incorrectly assigns the known value directly to cal_offset instead of computing the offset as the difference between the known value and current reading.

testcases.title: Buggy Protected Access Qualifier Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates a common bug in SystemVerilog class inheritance where a derived class (VideoPlayer or AudioPlayer) shadows a parent's protected member by re-declaring it with the same name. The override method writes to the shadow variable instead of the parent's protected state, leaving the parent's state unchanged and breaking encapsulation.

testcases.title: Buggy Constant Class Properties Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates const property initialization in SystemVerilog classes, where const properties must be initialized either at declaration or in the constructor. The buggy code fails to properly initialize const properties in the constructor and the child class, leading to compilation/initialization errors.

testcases.title: Buggy Constant Class Properties Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates const property initialization in SystemVerilog classes, including class constants, const parameters in constructors, and const arrays. The code contains multiple bugs where const properties are either not properly initialized or used incorrectly in inheritance hierarchies.

testcases.title: Buggy Typedef Class In Sv Ex1
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog exercise demonstrating circular class references using typedef class forward declarations. The SList container class and ListNode element class reference each other, but a critical bug causes the parent_list back-reference to remain null because append() and prepend() pass null instead of 'this' when constructing nodes.

testcases.title: Buggy Typedef Class In Sv Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog class exercise demonstrating typedef class forward declarations for bidirectional observer pattern. The EventEmitter class incorrectly creates a new shadow EventHandler object in attach() instead of wiring the caller-supplied handler directly, leaving the original handler's back-reference (source) null and breaking the circular reference.

testcases.title: Systemverilog Modport
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates SystemVerilog modport definitions for directional signal access control in interfaces. Shows how to define master and slave modports within a parameterized bus interface, controlling which signals are inputs, outputs, or inouts from each perspective. This enforces protocol compliance by preventing illegal signal access patterns at compile time.

testcases.title: Systemverilog Clocking Block
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates SystemVerilog clocking blocks for race-condition-free testbench-DUT communication, featuring timing-safe signal sampling and driving with configurable input/output skews. Shows interface-based clocking with cycle delays using the ## operator for synchronous stimulus and response.

testcases.title: Virtual Interface
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates virtual interfaces in SystemVerilog for connecting class-based testbench components to physical interfaces. Shows BFM implementation patterns, interface instantiation, and the separation between interface definition and testbench class usage.

testcases.title: Buggy Interface Exercise1
testcases.scenario: SPI bus interface with modports and clocking blocks contains a critical bug in the slave clocking block where sclk and mosi are incorrectly marked as inputs instead of being properly defined, preventing correct slave-side signal synchronization. The master modport also mixes input/output signals incorrectly in the clocking block, causing port direction mismatches that will prevent proper master-slave communication.

testcases.title: Buggy Interface Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Wishbone bus interface with modports and clocking blocks, featuring master/slave communication patterns in SystemVerilog. The design contains intentional bugs in syntax and task definition that prevent proper compilation and execution.

testcases.title: Buggy Systemverilog Modport Ex1
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog interface with modport declarations for master, slave, and monitor perspectives on a simple bus protocol. The master initiates read transactions while the slave services them, but the master's read enable logic contains a bug that prevents proper read operations.

testcases.title: Buggy Systemverilog Modport Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates a critical modport direction error where the slave modport incorrectly declares the handshake signal 'ready' as an input instead of an output. Since the slave is the sole driver of the ready signal, this declaration prevents the slave from writing to ready, causing it to remain undriven (X/0) and breaking the master-slave handshake protocol.

testcases.title: Buggy Systemverilog Clocking Block Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates SystemVerilog clocking blocks in a testbench-DUT interface with a memory controller. The driver class uses clocking block events to synchronize read/write operations, but contains an incomplete read() task that will cause compilation failure or incorrect behavior.

testcases.title: Buggy Systemverilog Clocking Block Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog clocking block interface for a memory controller with driver and monitor, demonstrating protocol handshaking. The exercise tests proper use of clocking block timing skews and protocol sequencing for read/write operations.

testcases.title: Buggy Virtual Interface Ex1
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog virtual interface exercise demonstrating the interaction between clocking blocks, modports, and driver classes. The DUT is a GPIO controller that captures input data and outputs a masked version based on direction pins, tested through a virtual interface driver.

testcases.title: Buggy Virtual Interface Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog virtual interface exercise where a GPIO driver incorrectly drives data_out through the clocking block instead of data_in, preventing the DUT from receiving the intended write data. The modport access restrictions and clocking block signal mapping create a subtle port mismatch that breaks the intended test stimulus.

testcases.title: Systemverilog Callback
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates SystemVerilog callback mechanisms including virtual method callbacks, callback registration/execution, and pre/post operation hooks. Illustrates the observer pattern and UVM-style callback methodology for building extensible verification environments.

testcases.title: Buggy Systemverilog Callback Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog driver class with callback hooks demonstrating pre/post drive callbacks for extensibility. The exercise contains three intentional bugs related to callback registration, parameter passing, and class syntax that prevent proper callback execution and data modification propagation.

testcases.title: Buggy Systemverilog Callback Exercise2
testcases.scenario: A monitor class implementing the observer pattern with virtual callbacks for notifying scoreboards and coverage collectors of transaction events. The design demonstrates callback-based verification but contains bugs in the comparison logic and incomplete error handler implementation.

testcases.title: Systemverilog Dpi
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates SystemVerilog Direct Programming Interface (DPI) for interfacing with C/C++ code, covering import and export declarations, DPI data types, context functions, pure functions, chandle pointers, string handling, and array passing mechanisms.

testcases.title: Buggy Systemverilog Dpi Exercise1
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog module demonstrating DPI-C function imports/exports with intentional bugs in declarations, function implementations, and testbench integration. The exercise tests understanding of DPI pure function constraints, proper argument passing, and function completeness.

testcases.title: Buggy Systemverilog Dpi Exercise2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog DPI export exercise where functions are tagged for C/DPI linkage. The sv_byte_reverse() function contains a bug where byte-swapped results are written to a local variable instead of the declared output parameter, causing callers to receive incorrect values.

testcases.title: If Else In Constraints
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates conditional constraint logic in SystemVerilog using if-else blocks within constraint definitions. Shows how to apply different randomization ranges based on mode selection and nested conditional constraints for address alignment.

testcases.title: Implication Operator
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the implication operator (->) in SystemVerilog constraints, showing how to establish conditional relationships between constrained variables. This example covers unidirectional implications (cmd determines addr range, valid determines data value) and bidirectional implications (<->) to enforce co-dependent constraint behaviors across randomized transactions.

testcases.title: Foreach Loop In Constraint
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates foreach loops in SystemVerilog constraints for applying rules across array elements. Shows constraint application on fixed/dynamic arrays, multidimensional arrays, and aggregate constraints like sum() checks with conditional logic.

testcases.title: Dist Keyword In Constraints
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the dist keyword for weighted probability distributions in SystemVerilog constraints, showing both := (individual weights) and :/ (range-divided weights) operators to control randomization probabilities across different signal values.

testcases.title: Inheritance In Constraint
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates constraint inheritance in SystemVerilog where derived classes inherit, override, and extend constraints from base classes across multiple levels of hierarchy. Shows how constraint names enable selective overriding while new constraints can reference both inherited and newly-defined random variables.

testcases.title: Function In Constraint
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates using user-defined functions within SystemVerilog constraints to enforce complex validation rules. Shows how functions enable reusable constraint logic for address validation, power-of-2 checking, checksum calculation, and conditional constraints based on command types.

testcases.title: Disable Randomization
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates three practical patterns for controlling randomization in SystemVerilog: disabling individual rand variables via rand_mode(), using constraints to implement selective randomization, and managing dynamic array randomization with transaction-like classes.

testcases.title: Static Constraints
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates static constraints in SystemVerilog, showing how constraint declaration with the 'static' keyword creates shared constraints across all instances of a class. When a static constraint is disabled on any instance, it affects all instances; instance constraints only affect their specific object.

testcases.title: Unique Constraint
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the unique constraint in SystemVerilog, which ensures all constrained elements are different. Shows unique constraints applied to arrays, individual fields, and complex scenarios combining unique with range constraints.

testcases.title: Bidirectional Constraint
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates bidirectional constraints in SystemVerilog where the constraint solver can work in multiple directions to satisfy relationships between random variables. Shows practical applications including arithmetic relationships (sum constraints), address calculations, and timing specifications.

testcases.title: Solve Before In Constraint
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates solve-before constraint ordering in SystemVerilog, where certain random variables are solved before others to enable conditional constraints and proper distribution. Shows two practical examples: mode-dependent address ranges and packet type-dependent field sizes.

testcases.title: Inline Constraints
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates inline constraints in SystemVerilog using the randomize() with {} construct to dynamically apply temporary constraints during randomization. Shows how to restrict random variables to specific ranges, values, and relationships without modifying base constraints.

testcases.title: Soft Constraint
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates soft constraints in SystemVerilog, which provide default randomized values that can be easily overridden by inline constraints. Shows how soft constraints enable flexible test scenarios while maintaining sensible defaults for rapid test development.

testcases.title: Randomization Methods
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates SystemVerilog randomization callbacks (pre_randomize and post_randomize) to manage derived data, constraint-based random generation, and state tracking across multiple randomization calls. Shows how pre/post hooks enable computing dependent values like checksums and sequence numbers without manual intervention.

testcases.title: Randcase In Sv
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the randcase statement in SystemVerilog for weighted random selection across multiple scenarios. Shows how to use randcase for generating random operations, addresses, and data patterns with specified probability weights that sum to 100%.

testcases.title: Buggy Randomization Exercise1
testcases.scenario: Network packet generator with constrained randomization demonstrating distribution weighting, implication constraints, and dynamic array sizing. Contains intentional bugs in constraint logic and weight distribution that cause incorrect randomization behavior.

testcases.title: Buggy Randomization Exercise2
testcases.scenario: Memory transaction class with randomization constraints designed to test solve-before ordering, soft constraints, and inline constraint overrides. The exercise contains intentional bugs in constraint declaration and ordering that prevent proper randomization of burst length based on command type.

testcases.title: Buggy If Else In Constraints Ex1
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog constraint exercise demonstrating if-else conditional constraints in randomization. The design attempts to implement mode-dependent constraints where data value determines valid address ranges and burst values, along with alignment constraints based on address ranges. Multiple constraint blocks use if-else logic to enforce conditional relationships between random variables.

testcases.title: Buggy If Else In Constraints Ex2
testcases.scenario: Exercise demonstrates if-else constraints in SystemVerilog randomization with multiple constraint blocks that should enforce relationships between packet fields. The design contains logical errors in constraint definitions that violate expected field relationships and create unsatisfiable constraints.

testcases.title: Buggy Implication Operator Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates the implication operator (->), a critical constraint construct in SystemVerilog randomization. The buggy code intentionally uses logical AND (&&) instead of implication in the write_c constraint, forcing both conditions to always be true rather than creating a conditional relationship between address and command.

testcases.title: Buggy Implication Operator Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates constraint implication operators in SystemVerilog randomization, specifically exposing a common over-constraining bug where a unidirectional implication (address[3:0]==0 -> opcode==OP_FLUSH) incorrectly forces FLUSH operations on all 16-byte-aligned addresses, rather than simply restricting FLUSH operations to aligned addresses.

testcases.title: Buggy Foreach Loop In Constraint Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates constraint solving failures caused by contradictory constraints and incorrect logical operators in SystemVerilog randomization. The design attempts to apply foreach loop constraints on arrays but contains logical errors that make the constraints unsatisfiable.

testcases.title: Buggy Foreach Loop In Constraint Ex2
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog randomization exercise with foreach loops in constraints that has multiple bugs preventing proper constraint enforcement. The exercise tests understanding of foreach constraint syntax, nested array constraints, and proper conditional logic within randomization.

testcases.title: Buggy Dist Keyword In Constraints Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates the dist keyword for weighted randomization across different value ranges and individual values. It tests proper syntax and weight interpretation for both single values (priority) and ranges (opcode and data), where incorrect use of ':=' vs ':/' operators causes distribution violations.

testcases.title: Buggy Dist Keyword In Constraints Ex2
testcases.scenario: Exercise demonstrates the dist keyword in SystemVerilog constraints with both weighted (:/=) and equal-frequency (:=) distributions. The buggy code contains a constraint syntax error where two dist constraints are applied to the same signal (delay), which is invalid in SystemVerilog.

testcases.title: Buggy Inheritance In Constraint Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates constraint inheritance in SystemVerilog where derived classes define constraints with the same name as parent classes, causing unintended constraint overriding rather than accumulation. The buggy design shows a three-level inheritance hierarchy (BasePkt → ExtPkt → PremPkt) where identically-named constraints in child classes silently replace parent constraints instead of being combined.

testcases.title: Buggy Inheritance In Constraint Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog constraint inheritance exercise where a derived class (ReadOnlyConfig) redefines a constraint from the base class (BaseConfig), but the redefined constraint does not inherit the alignment requirement (reg_addr[1:0]==0). This tests whether students understand that constraint redefinition overrides parent constraints rather than extending them.

testcases.title: Buggy Function In Constraint Ex1
testcases.scenario: Exercise demonstrates using functions within SystemVerilog constraints for complex validation logic. The randomizer must ensure constraints that invoke helper functions are satisfied, testing the constraint solver's ability to handle procedural logic.

testcases.title: Buggy Function In Constraint Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise tests constraint solving with functions that compute derived values. The randomizer must call get_region(), is_even(), and calc_parity() functions within constraints to ensure address maps to correct region, data is even, and parity bits are correctly calculated.

testcases.title: Buggy Disable Randomization Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates a critical randomization control bug where calling rand_mode(0) at the object level freezes ALL random fields instead of disabling randomization for only the addr field. The testbench expects addr to remain constant while data and cmd continue to randomize after lock_addr() is called, but the bug prevents any fields from changing.

testcases.title: Buggy Disable Randomization Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates a critical randomization bug where post_randomize() unconditionally re-randomizes the 'data' field by calling $urandom_range(), completely bypassing any rand_mode(0) freeze that a test may have applied. The bug shows how post_randomize() hooks can inadvertently defeat disable_randomization constraints, re-freezing previously locked fields.

testcases.title: Buggy Static Constraints Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates static constraints in SystemVerilog randomization, where students must identify why static constraints are not properly restricting random values across class instances. The testbench validates that addr, data, and cmd fields stay within their specified ranges through repeated randomization.

testcases.title: Buggy Static Constraints Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates static constraints in SystemVerilog randomization, where multiple constraint objects share class-level constraints that apply to all instances. The code intends to randomize a PoolItem class with static constraints on id and type_id ranges, plus an instance constraint on value being non-zero.

testcases.title: Buggy Unique Constraint Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates a constraint satisfaction conflict where a unique constraint on an 8-element array of 4-bit values cannot be satisfied when the value range is restricted to [0:5], providing only 6 possible unique values for 8 array elements. The testbench expects randomization to fail due to this impossible constraint combination.

testcases.title: Buggy Unique Constraint Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates a common constraint contradiction where a unique constraint is applied to an array larger than the domain it's constrained to. The code attempts to randomize 6 unique slot values from a range of only [1:5], which is mathematically impossible (6 values cannot be unique within 5 possible values).

testcases.title: Buggy Bidirectional Constraint Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise tests bidirectional constraint solving in SystemVerilog, where the solver must satisfy ordering constraints (a≤b≤c), range constraints on each variable, and a dependent constraint (sum=a+b+c) simultaneously. The bug prevents the constraint solver from finding valid solutions that satisfy all constraints together.

testcases.title: Buggy Bidirectional Constraint Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog class with bidirectional constraints on memory address range. The constraint range_c incorrectly computes end_addr as base_addr + length instead of base_addr + length - 1, causing the address range to be off-by-one and violating the intended inclusive endpoint calculation.

testcases.title: Buggy Solve Before In Constraint Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise tests the solve_before constraint ordering directive in SystemVerilog randomization. The constraint attempts to solve the mode variable before len to enable conditional constraints on len based on mode's value, but there is a critical syntax error that prevents the code from compiling.

testcases.title: Buggy Solve Before In Constraint Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates how solve-before ordering affects the marginal distribution of constrained random variables. With the bug (solve length before pkt_type), length is drawn uniformly first and pkt_type is forced by the range constraints, making pkt_type==0 appear in only ~25% of trials instead of the intended ~50%. Fixing the order ensures pkt_type is drawn first (uniform 0/1), then length is constrained to the matching range.

testcases.title: Buggy Inline Constraints Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise tests inline constraint randomization in SystemVerilog. The testbench attempts to constrain random variables using the 'with' clause during randomize() calls, but there is a constraint conflict: the class-level mode_c constraint forces mode==2'b01, while Test 4 tries to inline a conflicting constraint mode==2'b10, which should cause randomization to fail.

testcases.title: Buggy Inline Constraints Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog randomization exercise demonstrating inline constraints with a packet-like class containing source/destination addresses, length, and priority fields. The exercise tests basic constraint solving and inline constraint overrides during randomization.

testcases.title: Buggy Soft Constraint Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates soft constraints in SystemVerilog randomization, where soft constraints provide default values that can be overridden by hard constraints or inline randomize directives. The testbench verifies that soft constraints are applied when no overriding constraints exist, and that inline constraints properly override soft defaults.

testcases.title: Buggy Soft Constraint Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates soft constraints in SystemVerilog randomization, where soft constraints provide default bias values that can be overridden by randomization or inline constraints. The testbench verifies that soft constraints guide randomization toward specified values while hard constraints remain inviolable.

testcases.title: Buggy Randomization Methods Ex1
testcases.scenario: A SystemVerilog class demonstrates randomization with pre/post hooks and constraints, but the checksum calculation uses addition instead of XOR, violating the test's expectation for proper error detection.

testcases.title: Buggy Randomization Methods Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise tests randomization methods in SystemVerilog, specifically pre_randomize() and post_randomize() hooks, along with constraints on dynamic arrays. The testbench checks that sequence numbering works correctly across multiple randomizations and that post_randomize properly sets values.

testcases.title: Buggy Randcase In Sv Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates the randcase statement in SystemVerilog for weighted random selection of operations. The design generates random operations (READ, WRITE, MODIFY, ERASE, NOP) with specified weight percentages and tracks their statistical distribution.

testcases.title: Buggy Randcase In Sv Ex2
testcases.scenario: SystemVerilog randcase statement with weights that sum to 100 but includes a zero-weight branch (IDLE with weight 0), causing it to never be selected during randomization. The exercise tests pattern generation, delay generation, and statistical distribution of random outcomes.

testcases.title: Cover Group
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates covergroup declaration and instantiation in SystemVerilog at both class and module scopes. Shows how covergroups encapsulate coverage specifications with coverpoints, and illustrates proper instantiation with the new() constructor and sampling methodology.

testcases.title: Sample
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates four complementary covergroup sampling methods in SystemVerilog: explicit sample() calls for manual control, event-based triggering for transaction capture, signal edge detection for protocol-aware sampling, and clock-based sampling for continuous monitoring. This example shows how to choose the appropriate sampling technique based on verification objectives.

testcases.title: Cover Points
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates coverpoint declaration in SystemVerilog, showing how to specify which variables to monitor for coverage, configure bins automatically, and set coverage goals/weights. Illustrates basic coverpoints, goal-based coverage targets, and weighted coverage metrics.

testcases.title: Coverpoint Expression
