testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the complete UVM testbench infrastructure required to start and execute sequences: an agent containing driver and sequencer, proper port connections, and a driver that processes sequence items through get_next_item/item_done handshaking. This example shows the foundational pattern for stimulus generation in UVM-based verification.

testcases.title: Uvmsequencerarbitration
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates a complete UVM agent with sequencer-driver arbitration, where the sequencer arbitrates between multiple sequences and delivers items to the driver in a controlled manner. The driver processes items sequentially and reports statistics, showcasing the fundamental producer-consumer pattern in UVM verification.

testcases.title: Uvmsequencerlockandgrab
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the UVM sequencer's lock() and grab() mechanisms by implementing a complete agent-driver-environment hierarchy where the driver uses get_next_item() to retrieve transactions and item_done() to signal completion, establishing the handshake protocol required for sequencer arbitration.

testcases.title: Uvmvirtualsequence
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates a complete UVM agent hierarchy for Core A, including sequencer-driver connection patterns and item-driven handshaking protocol. Illustrates proper component instantiation, phasing discipline, and monitoring of driven items through report_phase.

testcases.title: Uvmsubscriber
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates a complete UVM testbench architecture with an agent containing driver, sequencer, and monitor, along with multiple subscribers (functional coverage, scoreboard, statistics) connected to the monitor's analysis port to receive broadcasted transactions.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmsubscriber Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM testbench with a monitor that writes mon_item transactions to an analysis port and a subscriber that should receive them. The subscriber's write() method increments a counter and logs each sample, but the analysis port is never connected to the subscriber in connect_phase, so no transactions flow through.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmsubscriber Exercise2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates UVM subscriber usage with multiple subscriber types filtering transaction streams. Students must identify inverted filter logic that counts wrong transaction types, a missing super.build_phase() call, and missing coverage reporting in the subscriber hierarchy.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlm Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM TLM testbench with a producer and consumer component where the producer attempts to put items through a blocking put port, but the connection between the port and the receiving FIFO is missing in the connect_phase, causing items to never be transferred.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlm Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM TLM exercise demonstrating analysis port connectivity issues where a dual-port subscriber has one analysis port properly connected and another left unconnected, resulting in zero items received on the disconnected port. The design uses UVM's analysis port and FIFO infrastructure but fails to establish complete dataflow paths.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmanalysisfifo Ex1
testcases.scenario: UVM TLM analysis port and import connection exercise where a producer sends tlm_items through an analysis_port to a consumer's analysis_imp. The code demonstrates the one-to-many broadcast pattern in UVM TLM but has a critical connectivity bug preventing communication.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmanalysisfifo Ex2
testcases.scenario: A UVM testbench demonstrating TLM analysis port/imp communication between a producer and consumer component. The producer generates random items and writes them through an analysis port, while the consumer receives them via an analysis implementation port and stores them in a queue.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmanalysisport Ex1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates UVM TLM (Transaction-Level Modeling) with analysis ports and imps, where a producer component fails to broadcast transactions through its analysis port to connected consumer components. Students must identify why received items remain empty despite the producer creating and randomizing transactions.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmanalysisport Ex2
testcases.scenario: A UVM testbench demonstrates TLM (Transaction Level Modeling) communication between a producer and consumer using uvm_analysis_port and uvm_analysis_imp. The producer generates random transactions and writes them via an analysis port, while the consumer receives and logs them.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmblockinggetport Ex1
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM producer-consumer testbench that attempts to use blocking get port/export for inter-component communication. The producer should send items to the consumer via a connected port, but the connection is never established in the environment's build_phase.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmblockinggetport Ex2
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM producer-consumer design where the producer attempts to use a blocking_get_port to retrieve items from a consumer, but the port is never instantiated in the build_phase. The consumer implements the get_imp interface and generates randomized items, but the producer cannot receive them due to the missing port initialization.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmblockingputport Ex1
testcases.scenario: UVM TLM blocking put port communication test between producer and consumer components. The producer sends randomized tlm_item objects through a blocking put port while the consumer receives them via a blocking put implementation, demonstrating point-to-point TLM connectivity.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmblockingputport Ex2
testcases.scenario: This design demonstrates UVM TLM blocking put port communication between a producer and consumer component. The producer generates random items and sends them via a blocking put port, while the consumer receives items through a blocking put implementation interface.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmnonblockinggetport Ex1
testcases.scenario: UVM TLM blocking get communication demonstrating producer-consumer pattern with port-imp connectivity. The design shows how a producer component should request data from a consumer via blocking get interface, but fails to properly establish the port-imp connection required for TLM transactions.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmnonblockinggetport Ex2
testcases.scenario: This UVM testbench demonstrates UVM TLM blocking get port/imp communication between a producer and consumer component, but fails to instantiate the consumer and connect the producer's get_port to the consumer's get_imp, breaking the communication channel.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmnonblockingputport Ex1
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM testbench demonstrating blocking put port communication between a producer and consumer component, but contains a syntax error that prevents compilation and execution of the communication flow.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmnonblockingputport Ex2
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM testbench demonstrating blocking put port communication between producer and consumer components. The code is incomplete with a truncated build_phase function in the tlm_env class, preventing proper port connection and environment instantiation.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlm Decl Ex1
testcases.scenario: UVM TLM blocking get port-imp connection exercise where the producer attempts to retrieve items from a consumer via a blocking get port, but the environment fails to instantiate child components and connect the port-imp pair.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlm Decl Ex2
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM testbench with producer and consumer components that demonstrates blocking get port/export communication. The producer should send items to the consumer via a connected TLM port-export pair, but the build_phase is incomplete, preventing proper port connection.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlmfifo Ex1
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM producer-consumer example where the producer attempts to send items via a blocking get port, but the port is never instantiated in build_phase, preventing any TLM communication. The consumer receives randomized items instead of the producer's actual data.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlmfifo Ex2
testcases.scenario: Producer-consumer UVM testbench using TLM blocking get port/implementation. The producer should send randomized items to the consumer through a TLM interface, but the build_phase is incomplete and the TLM connection is never established.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlmsockets Ex1
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM testbench with a producer and consumer component that uses blocking get ports for inter-component communication. The producer attempts to send items to the consumer, but the TLM connection between them is never established, causing the communication to fail.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlmsockets Ex2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates UVM TLM blocking socket communication between a producer and consumer component. The producer attempts to send items via a blocking get port, while the consumer implements the get interface, but the port-to-export connection in the environment's build phase is missing.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlmtime Ex1
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM producer-consumer testbench where the producer attempts to send items to the consumer via blocking get port/imp, but fails to establish the TLM connection. The producer creates and randomizes items but never actually passes them through the TLM interface to the consumer.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmtlmtime Ex2
testcases.scenario: A UVM TLM exercise where a producer component attempts to send items to a consumer via blocking get ports, but the TLM connection between producer and consumer is never established. The producer sends data but the consumer never receives it because the port-to-implementation connection is missing from the environment's build_phase.

testcases.title: Uvmanalysisfifo
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM TLM analysis FIFO pattern where a faster producer broadcasts transactions via uvm_analysis_port, and a slower consumer receives them through uvm_tlm_analysis_fifo that buffers the data. The FIFO decouples producer and consumer timing, preventing data loss when production rate exceeds consumption rate.

testcases.title: Uvmanalysisport
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM TLM communication using blocking put ports and analysis ports for one-to-many broadcast. ComponentA sends packets via uvm_blocking_put_port to componentB, which receives them through uvm_blocking_put_imp and broadcasts to multiple subscribers via uvm_analysis_port.

testcases.title: Uvmblockinggetport
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates blocking TLM get communication where componentB requests packets via uvm_blocking_get_port and blocks until componentA's get() task completes. Shows how blocking get provides on-demand data transfer with implicit synchronization between sender and receiver.

testcases.title: Uvmblockingputport
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM blocking TLM communication using uvm_blocking_put_port and uvm_blocking_put_imp, where the master component sends memory transactions to a slave component and blocks until the slave completes processing each request, modeling realistic latency-based slave behavior.

testcases.title: Uvmnonblockinggetport
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM non-blocking TLM get communication between two components using uvm_nonblocking_get_imp (sender) and uvm_nonblocking_get_port (receiver). The try_get() function returns immediately without blocking, enabling the receiver to handle rejections and implement retry logic independently.

testcases.title: Uvmnonblockingputport
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM non-blocking TLM communication using uvm_nonblocking_put_port and uvm_nonblocking_put_imp, where a producer component sends transactions to a consumer without blocking, using try_put() for immediate acceptance/rejection and can_put() for readiness checks. The example shows producer retry logic, consumer acceptance probabilistically, and full transaction metadata tracking across both communicating components.

testcases.title: Uvmtlmfifo
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM TLM FIFO communication between a fast producer (componentA) and slow consumer (componentB) using blocking put/get ports. Shows how the FIFO automatically synchronizes mismatched data rates and blocks components when the buffer is full or empty.

testcases.title: Uvmtlmsockets
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates TLM 2.0 socket-based communication in UVM with both blocking (b_transport) and non-blocking (nb_transport) initiator implementations, showing proper socket instantiation, configuration database integration, and phase-based execution patterns.

testcases.title: Uvmtlmtime
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates how UVM TLM time (uvm_tlm_time) preserves precision across different timescales, contrasting with regular SystemVerilog 'time' which loses unit information when crossing timescale boundaries. The example shows two approaches: one using basic 'time' that suffers precision loss, and another using uvm_tlm_time with explicit unit specification for correct cross-timescale operation.

testcases.title: Decl
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM TLM blocking put port declaration and usage with multiple implementation ports. Shows how to use `uvm_blocking_put_imp_decl` macros to create separate put implementation ports in a receiver component that handles packets from multiple senders.

testcases.title: Uvmclone
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM clone() method usage across multiple transaction classes, showing basic cloning with field macros, clone vs copy differences, nested object cloning, and practical scoreboard usage patterns. Emphasizes the critical distinction between shallow copy() and deep clone() operations in verification environments.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmclone Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM clone operation with multiple defects: missing $cast for clone() return, unimplemented do_copy method, and shallow copy of nested objects. The test attempts to clone a my_txn object containing an inner_obj handle and verify that all fields including nested object values are properly replicated.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmclone Exercise2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates UVM object creation and cloning mechanics, specifically testing the differences between new(), create(), copy(), and clone() methods. It intentionally contains bugs related to shallow vs. deep cloning of dynamic structures (queues) and incorrect object instantiation patterns.

testcases.title: Uvmcompare
testcases.scenario: Comprehensive UVM comparison techniques demonstration covering field automation macros, UVM_NOCOMPARE flag, do_compare() callbacks, nested object comparison, and dynamic array comparison. This design teaches best practices for implementing custom comparison logic in UVM transaction classes.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcompare Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM object comparison test that demonstrates field registration and comparison logic. The exercise contains three bugs: (1) status field is not registered in uvm_object_utils, causing it to be excluded from comparisons, (2) the first compare() call uses == 0 instead of logical negation, and (3) mismatched field flags between rand and non-rand declarations lead to inconsistent comparison behavior.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcompare Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM transaction comparator with multiple bugs: do_compare() missing super call allowing incorrect comparisons, data field incorrectly marked with UVM_NOCOMPARE preventing automatic comparison, and custom do_compare logic that only checks address field while ignoring data values.

testcases.title: Uvmcomparer
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM comparer class functionality for comparing transactions and objects using various comparison methods (compare_field, compare_field_int, compare_string, compare_object) with policy-based filtering (UVM_DEEP, UVM_SHALLOW) and physical/abstract field classification.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcomparer Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM Comparer exercise demonstrating custom configuration impact on mismatch detection and reporting. Students must identify three interdependent bugs: show_max=0 suppressing mismatch output, sev=UVM_INFO preventing error classification, and inverted result logic masking failures.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcomparer Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM scoreboard that manually compares transactions instead of using the uvm_comparer utility, resulting in incomplete field verification and missed mismatches. The design creates a comparer object but never uses it, and only checks opcode and operand while ignoring the result field.

testcases.title: Uvmcopy
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM copy() methods across multiple implementation approaches: field automation macros for nested objects, do_copy() callbacks for performance optimization, and deep copy verification techniques. Shows practical patterns for transaction object copying in UVM testbenches.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcopy Exercise1
testcases.scenario: A UVM object copy exercise demonstrating three common pitfalls: calling copy() on a null target object, failing to invoke super.do_copy() in the overridden do_copy() method, and not properly deep-copying dynamic array fields. The test creates a frame object, copies it to another frame, and verifies that all fields (header, payload, crc) are correctly duplicated.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcopy Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM copy operation with nested objects where the copy direction is reversed, shallow copy is incorrectly applied to nested objects, and the nested object is not properly instantiated in the constructor. Students must identify that c1.copy(c2) copies c2 into c1 (not the other way around), that UVM_SHALLOW prevents deep copying of nested objects, and that uninitialized nested objects cause null pointer issues.

testcases.title: Uvmpackunpack
testcases.scenario: Comprehensive demonstration of UVM pack/unpack mechanisms including field automation macros, do_pack/do_unpack callbacks, nested object packing, and dynamic array handling. Covers both basic transactions and advanced serialization patterns essential for verification testbenches.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmpackunpack Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM pack/unpack exercise demonstrating field ordering issues and missing super calls. The design attempts to pack and unpack a packet object with header, address, data, and CRC fields, but contains mismatched field orders between pack and unpack operations, missing super.do_pack() call, and incorrect bit width in unpack.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmpackunpack Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM pack/unpack exercise demonstrating custom packing of mixed-size fields including an 8-bit header, variable-length byte array payload, and 16-bit checksum. Students must identify why the packed bit array size is incorrect and trace the root cause in the do_pack() override.

testcases.title: Uvmprint
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM print() methods across multiple transaction classes using field automation macros, do_print() callbacks, and nested object printing. Shows proper class hierarchy, macro-based field registration, and different printer output formats for comprehensive transaction visibility.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmprint Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates three common bugs in UVM object printing: missing field registration in the utility macro, incomplete do_print override that doesn't call super, and fields that won't appear in print output due to these omissions. Students must identify why the 'desc' field disappears from prints and why the internal_id field is missing from custom do_print output.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmprint Exercise2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates UVM printer configuration for objects and components, specifically testing how recursion depth affects nested object printing and highlighting deprecated knobs API usage in modern UVM.

testcases.title: Uvmsingletonobject
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the UVM Singleton design pattern using static instance variables and factory methods to ensure only one object instance exists across the testbench. Shows both a basic singleton_obj class and a singleton_config class with proper get_instance() and reset_instance() methods for controlled object lifecycle.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmsingletonobject Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This UVM singleton pattern implementation creates multiple instances instead of maintaining a single shared object, causing configuration changes made by one component to be invisible to others. The exercise demonstrates how missing singleton enforcement (static handle, protected constructor) leads to independent object creation on each call to get_inst().

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmsingletonobject Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM singleton pattern implementation where get_inst() fails to cache the singleton instance and instead creates a new instance on every call, breaking the fundamental singleton guarantee that only one instance should exist throughout simulation.

testcases.title: Uvmbarrier
testcases.scenario: Comprehensive UVM testbench demonstrating UVM Barrier for multi-process synchronization, including threshold management, waiter tracking, reset behavior, and auto-reset functionality across multiple test scenarios.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmbarrier Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This UVM testbench demonstrates barrier synchronization where multiple components should wait at a barrier before proceeding. The design contains configuration and implementation bugs that prevent proper synchronization.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmbarrier Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM testbench with three synchronization bugs in barrier usage: missing auto_reset configuration, reset() called at improper phase, and barrier threshold modified after components are active. Students must identify why the barrier fails to reset between passes and workers hang.

testcases.title: Uvmcallbacks
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM callback pattern implementation with package organization, callback base classes, and agent structure. Shows how to encapsulate driver and sequence callbacks for runtime behavior modification without changing component source code.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcallbacks Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM callbacks exercise demonstrating driver-level callback registration and execution. The design shows a callback-based error injection mechanism where callbacks should modify transaction data before and after driver operations, but contains critical registration and initialization bugs that prevent callbacks from executing.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcallbacks Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM testbench with callback registration and invocation issues. Students must identify why callback instances are not properly executing their functionality, diagnose ordering problems during callback registration, and spot method signature mismatches between base and derived callback classes.

testcases.title: Uvmcommandlineprocessor
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates the UVM command line processor (uvm_cmdline_processor) singleton class and its key methods for accessing command-line arguments and plusargs at runtime. This example shows how to retrieve and process various types of command-line inputs without recompilation, enabling flexible test configuration and parameterization.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcommandlineprocessor Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates common mistakes when using UVM's command-line processor: misinterpreting get_arg_value() return semantics (returns count, not the parsed string value), using incorrect plusarg prefix syntax (missing '+' character), and failing to initialize signals when command-line arguments are absent.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmcommandlineprocessor Exercise2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates improper use of UVM's command line processor APIs for parsing multiple arguments and array values. The code attempts to extract test names and iteration counts from command line arguments but fails to correctly utilize get_arg_matches() results and misuses get_arg_value() for array population.

testcases.title: Uvmevent
testcases.scenario: UVM Event synchronization mechanism with transaction-based data passing and callback support. Demonstrates how uvm_event#(T) enables inter-process communication with persistent triggering to avoid race conditions, including custom callback registration and comprehensive test coverage for all event methods.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmevent Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM Event synchronization between producer and consumer components demonstrating event pool retrieval, trigger/wait sequencing, and event lifecycle management. The design attempts to coordinate data availability signals but contains multiple implementation errors that prevent proper event synchronization.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmevent Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM event exercise demonstrating event data passing and callback handling. The test creates an event with data payload and callback, then triggers the event in a fork while the main thread waits and retrieves the triggered data.

testcases.title: Uvmheartbeat
testcases.scenario: UVM testbench demonstrating the uvm_heartbeat watchdog mechanism for monitoring component liveness through objection-based heartbeat tracking. Shows how to configure heartbeat monitoring modes (ALL_ACTIVE, ONE_ACTIVE, ANY_ACTIVE) and implement components that raise objections at configurable rates to maintain heartbeat signals.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmheartbeat Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This UVM heartbeat monitoring exercise demonstrates component synchronization through heartbeat objections. The design creates multiple components that pulse at regular intervals while the environment manages a heartbeat object for coordinating their activity.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmheartbeat Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM testbench with a heartbeat monitor that should detect timeout when a monitored component stops pulsing. The test creates a pulse component that raises/drops objections periodically, but configuration errors prevent proper heartbeat monitoring and timeout detection.

testcases.title: Uvmpool
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM Pool functionality including global event pool access, inter-component synchronization via shared events, and the complete UVM testbench infrastructure. Shows how to retrieve and use pooled objects (uvm_event) across multiple components using get_global() for shared resource management.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmpool Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This buggy exercise demonstrates UVM Pool global instance management, where the producer adds key-value pairs to the global pool but the consumer fails to retrieve them due to three distinct bugs: creating a new pool instance instead of accessing the global pool, using a mismatched key name, and checking for a non-existent key.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmpool Exercise2
testcases.scenario: This UVM Pool exercise demonstrates object pool management with three intentional bugs: (1) dereferencing a null object returned by pool.get() on a missing key, (2) deleting an entry during forward iteration which corrupts the iterator state, and (3) incomplete code in the report_phase function. Students must identify unsafe pool operations and proper iteration/deletion patterns.

testcases.title: Uvmqueue
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM Queue as a parameterized dynamic data structure with producer and consumer components exchanging string items. Illustrates core queue operations including push_front, push_back, insert, pop_front, pop_back, size, and global queue access patterns.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmqueue Exercise1
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates UVM queue operations including global queue access, push/pop semantics, and size checking. Students must identify bugs in queue sharing between references, LIFO vs FIFO pop behavior, and off-by-one errors in queue size validation.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmqueue Exercise2
testcases.scenario: UVM Queue-based scoreboard that tracks expected vs. actual values using FIFO semantics. The exercise exposes three critical bugs: missing empty queue validation before pop, off-by-one indexing in peek operations, and lack of queue reset between consecutive test runs.

testcases.title: Uvmresourcedb
testcases.scenario: Demonstrates UVM resource database techniques including basic set/read operations, priority-based overrides, struct-based feature flags, and scoped resource access. Shows proper resource lifecycle and retrieval patterns within component hierarchies.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmresourcedb Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM ResourceDB exercise demonstrating resource set/get operations with multiple bugs including type mismatches between resource writes and reads, scope specification errors, and confusion between set_default and set APIs that prevent proper resource retrieval.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmresourcedb Exercise2
testcases.scenario: This exercise demonstrates a common UVM ResourceDB misunderstanding where read_by_type is used to retrieve a specific named resource, which returns the first matching resource of that type rather than the intended val_b resource. The test fails because read_by_type doesn't guarantee which int resource is returned, and the debug dump() call is commented out, preventing visibility into the actual resource database state.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmral Exercise1
testcases.scenario: UVM RAL register model with three critical bugs: incorrect field access policies (RO instead of RW), misaligned register map offset, and missing HDL path configuration for simulation-to-RTL synchronization.

testcases.title: Buggy Uvmral Exercise2
testcases.scenario: This UVM RAL exercise demonstrates register model configuration with adapter and predictor connectivity. The design attempts to create a simple register block with a data register and an adapter, but fails to properly implement the adapter's reg2bus conversion and omits the predictor connection, preventing accurate register prediction and bus-to-register synchronization.

testcases.title: Src
testcases.scenario: GPIO controller module demonstrating APB-like register interface implementation with control, status, output, and interrupt registers. Showcases proper parameterization of register addresses, signal organization, and hierarchical port naming conventions for bus-based peripherals.

testcases.title: Agents
testcases.scenario: UVM agent for GPIO controller verification that demonstrates the standard agent architecture pattern, encapsulating a sequencer, driver, and monitor. The driver implements APB protocol transactions while the monitor passively observes interface activity, and the agent provides configuration to operate in either active (with stimulus generation) or passive modes.

testcases.title: Assertions
testcases.scenario: This module demonstrates SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) for formal property verification of a GPIO controller using the bind construct. It illustrates how to organize assertions by functional area (output, output enable, input synchronization, interrupts, reset, and stability) and implement property-based checking without modifying RTL code.

testcases.title: Env
testcases.scenario: Comprehensive UVM RAL-based GPIO controller verification environment demonstrating real-time signal checking, functional coverage collection, and register abstraction layer integration with explicit predictor-based scoreboarding.

testcases.title: Interface
testcases.scenario: APB-compatible interface for GPIO controller verification, providing signal-level connections between UVM testbench and DUT with standardized 2-phase transaction protocol (Setup and Access phases) for read/write operations.

testcases.title: Ral
testcases.scenario: UVM RAL adapter that converts abstract register operations into APB bus transactions, demonstrating the critical role of adapters in the Register Abstraction Layer architecture for GPIO controller register access.

testcases.title: Sequences
testcases.scenario: UVM sequence library for GPIO controller RAL verification that encapsulates test scenarios using the Register Abstraction Layer. Demonstrates organizing sequences by RAL feature testing (basic register access, field-level operations, mirror functionality, backdoor operations, and advanced RAL methods) to systematically verify register behavior through abstraction layers.

testcases.title: Tb
testcases.scenario: Top-level testbench module demonstrating UVM RAL (Register Abstraction Layer) verification infrastructure for a GPIO controller. This example shows proper clock/reset generation, virtual interface instantiation, DUT integration, and UVM test environment setup in SystemVerilog.

testcases.title: Tests
testcases.scenario: UVM test library for GPIO controller verification demonstrating comprehensive test organization across basic register operations, RAL (Register Abstraction Layer) functionality, and advanced verification techniques. This library serves as the test harness reference implementation showing how to structure multiple test classes for complete GPIO and RAL coverage.
